name: opensky-traffic-viz

name: wbgapi
what_it_holds: Python client (177 stars, actively maintained, on PyPI/conda-forge) for the World Bank's official Data API. Pulls any World Development Indicators series by country/year in a pandas-friendly way, including ST.INT.ARVL (international tourism, number of arrivals) and ST.INT.DPRT (departures) and ST.INT.RCPT (tourism receipts) for essentially every country back to the mid-1990s (UNWTO-sourced via WDI) -- covers Mexico, Brazil, Thailand, Indonesia, India, Korea, Japan, Australia, Canada all in one call, annual frequency.
why_useful: One-command, no-API-key acquisition of UNWTO-sourced annual international arrivals for every APAC/LatAm market named in gap #7, and a general macro/consumer cross-check tool for other themes. Annual only (not monthly), so it complements rather than replaces NTTO/JNTO/KTO monthly series, but is the fastest way to backfill any missing country-year and to sanity-check UNWTO totals without scraping unwto.org directly.

name: chicago-taxi-data
what_it_holds: Scripts to download and analyze City of Chicago taxi trip records (~200M rows as of Q1 2020) and Transportation Network Provider/TNP data (Uber/Lyft, ~130M rows), plus census-tract/community-area mapping, weather data, and shapefiles. Data pulled from Chicago's open-data portal (70GB+ CSV), not committed.
why_useful: Second major US metro ground-travel/rideshare volume series for gap #10; Chicago is a top-10 US market with international airport connections (O'Hare), useful as a cross-check on the NYC TLC series for broader US travel-demand read-through.

name: uber-tlc-foil-response
what_it_holds: FiveThirtyEight's classic FOIL-request dataset from NYC TLC: uber-raw-data-apr14.csv through sep14.csv (6 monthly files, ~4.5M Uber pickups Apr-Sep 2014, lat/lon/base), uber-raw-data-janjune-15.csv.zip (14.3M Uber pickups Jan-Jun 2015 with dispatching/affiliated base + location ID), Uber-Jan-Feb-FOIL.csv (aggregated daily Uber stats Jan-Feb 2015), and other-FHV-data/ covering 10 other NYC for-hire-vehicle companies plus other-FHV-data-jan-aug-2015.csv (daily pickups, 329 FHV companies, Jan-Aug 2015). NYC only, CC-BY-4.0 (parent fivethirtyeight/data repo), 735 stars, last updated Aug 2026 (repo itself, not the data vintage which is 2014-15).
why_useful: Point-in-time historical rideshare-volume snapshot for NYC predating most modern coverage; static and fully committed so it is trivially reproducible without a live pull, useful as an older baseline/backtest period for a ground-travel demand proxy (gap #10).
